title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
text:
Early in his reign, young King Solomon went to Gibeon, the great high place, and offered a thousand burnt offerings there. That night God appeared to him in a dream and said: "Ask what I shall give you."

Solomon began by remembering the kindness God had shown his father David. Then he spoke about himself. He was king in his father's place, he said, but he was only a little child who did not know how to go out or come in. He was in the middle of a great people, too many to be counted. So he asked for one thing: an understanding heart to judge the people and to tell good from bad. Otherwise, he asked, who could govern so great a people?

The request pleased God. Because Solomon had not asked for long life, or riches, or the death of his enemies, but for understanding to do justice, he would receive a wise and discerning heart, greater than anyone's before or after him. And he would also receive what he had not asked for: riches and honor beyond any other king of his time.

Solomon woke and knew it had been a dream. He returned to Jerusalem, stood before the Ark of the Covenant, offered sacrifices, and held a feast for all his servants.
lesson: When you take on responsibility for others, admit what you do not know and ask first for the ability to do the job well. Status and rewards tend to follow competence, not the reverse.
